intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September from London

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and arches along the golden coastline, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's dramatic geology.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Visit a local winery in the Lagoa wine region, the heart of Algarve viticulture, for a guided tasting of regional wines including Arinto and Negra Mole varieties. Pair your wines with a traditional Cataplana seafood stew prepared by a local chef.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park spanning 60km of coastline. Discover barrier islands, flamingo colonies, and secluded barrier beaches only accessible by boat, with stops for swimming and snorkeling in calm lagoon waters.

experiences.name: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the Moorish red sandstone castle of Silves, the ancient Algarve capital, followed by a guided food walk through the historic old town. Sample local specialties including carob products, medronho brandy, almond sweets, and fresh orange juice at traditional market stalls.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Eva Bus or Rede Expressos coach from Faro Airport to Lagos (approx. €5-7, ~1.5 hrs). Check into Boutique Taghostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva. Freshen up and get settled.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snack
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snack
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a nearby 24h mini-market or vending machine near the hostel — keep it simple tonight

day_by_day.notes: Bus from Faro to Lagos runs until late evening. Book ticket in advance at rede-expressos.pt. Taghostel is a short walk or cheap taxi (~€5) from Lagos bus station. Get rest — big day tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, enjoy a free self-guided walk through Lagos Old Town. Explore the historic city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone streets. Visit the free exterior of Igreja de Santo António.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia Beach (a 20-min walk or short bus ride, ~€1.50). This long, wide sandy beach is perfect for a first Algarve swim. Rent a beach umbrella and chair for ~€5-8. Enjoy the warm September sea.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Lagos marina at sunset. Explore the lively Rua 25 de Abril for budget dining options. Enjoy the relaxed evening atmosphere of Lagos town center.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mulher de Capote near the hostel — coffee + pastel de nata for ~€2
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach: grab fresh bread, local cheese, cured meats, and fruit from Mercado Municipal de Lagos (~€5 total)
meals.dinner: O Camilo or a local tasca on Rua 25 de Abril — prato do dia (dish of the day) with soup, main, and drink for ~€8-10

day_by_day.notes: September weather in Algarve is still warm (24-28°C) with less crowds than August. Sunscreen is essential. The hostel may offer free maps of Lagos.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning walk to Ponta da Piedade — Lagos's most iconic sea stack and grotto formation. It's a free 30-min walk from the hostel or a short taxi (~€6). Arrive early to beat any crowds and enjoy the dramatic golden cliffs in morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a kayak or join a budget group boat tour from Lagos marina to explore the sea caves and grottos up close (~€15-20 for a group tour). This is one of the best value experiences in the Algarve. Return to Praia do Camilo (small but stunning beach near Ponta da Piedade) for a swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos town. Visit the Mercado de Escravos (Slave Market Museum) — entry ~€3 — one of the world's first slave markets, historically significant. Walk the evening passeio along the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast if included, or local café — toast, juice, coffee for ~€3
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia do Camilo — grilled sardine sandwich and a beer for ~€6-8
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina near the marina — grilled fish or cataplana for ~€10-12

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat/kayak tour the day before at the marina to secure a spot. Wear water shoes for rocky beach access at Praia do Camilo.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres — take the Eva Bus from Lagos bus station (~€4 each way, 1 hr). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry), a 15th-century fortress at the southwestern tip of Europe. Walk the clifftop trails with stunning Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or hitch to Praia do Beliche or Praia da Mareta in Sagres — wild, windswept beaches popular with surfers. Enjoy the raw, unspoiled beauty. Watch local surfers ride the Atlantic swells.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Freshen up at the hostel. Head out for a Friday evening in Lagos — the town comes alive with travelers and locals. Explore the bar scene on Rua 25 de Abril.

meals.breakfast: Quick café stop in Lagos before the bus — coffee and croissant ~€2.50
meals.lunch: Sagres town center — Restaurante A Tasca or local snack bar, fresh tuna steak for ~€9-11
meals.dinner: Nah Nah Bah burger bar in Lagos — great value burgers and craft beer for ~€10-12

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September — bring a light layer. The bus schedule from Lagos to Sagres runs several times daily; check Eva Bus timetable. Sagres is the surfing capital of Portugal.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Take a morning bus or arrange a shared taxi to Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (~30 min from Lagos, ~€15 taxi or bus + walk). This Algarve winery offers affordable tasting sessions (~€10-15) with local red, white, and rosé wines amid beautiful vineyard scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine theme with a visit to a local wine shop in Lagos — Garrafeira do Mercado near the market. Pick up a bottle of local Algarve wine (Vida Nova or Quinta do Barranco Longo) for ~€6-8. Relax at Meia Praia Beach with your wine and a good book.
day_by_day.evening: Saturday night in Lagos — join the hostel social scene or meet fellow travelers. Head to Rua 25 de Abril for drinks. Many bars offer happy hour deals (2-for-1 cocktails, cheap shots).

meals.breakfast: Hostel or local padaria — fresh bread, butter, jam, coffee ~€3
meals.lunch: Winery picnic or light lunch at the winery café if available (~€8-10), or pack your own from the market
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — traditional Portuguese petiscos (tapas-style) for sharing, ~€10-12 per person

day_by_day.notes: Call ahead to book the winery tasting — Quinta dos Vales: +351 282 431 036. September is harvest season in the Algarve — you may see grape picking in action!

day_by_day.morning: Lazy Sunday morning — sleep in or do yoga on the hostel rooftop if available. Head to Praia de Porto de Mós, a beautiful and less-crowded beach a 30-min walk from Lagos. Enjoy the golden cliffs and clear water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rock formations and natural arches along the coastal walking trail between Porto de Mós and Ponta da Piedade. This free 2-3 km clifftop walk offers some of the most spectacular scenery in the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Sunday evening market browse if any local markets are running. Relax at the hostel common area, meet other travelers, and plan the week ahead. Early night to recharge.

meals.breakfast: Café Central in Lagos town square — full Portuguese breakfast (eggs, bread, juice, coffee) ~€5
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Porto de Mós — fresh salad and grilled chicken wrap ~€7
meals.dinner: Self-catering at the hostel — buy ingredients from Pingo Doce supermarket (pasta, sauce, salad) for ~€4-5 total. Great way to save money!

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is a great day for a slower pace. Supermarkets like Pingo Doce and Lidl in Lagos are budget lifesavers — stock up on snacks, water, and picnic supplies.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha. Take the train from Lagos to Portimão (~€2.50, 20 min — one of the cheapest and most scenic rail routes). Walk to Praia da Rocha, a wide golden beach with dramatic red rock formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Portimão town — visit the free Museu de Portimão (free on Sundays, €3 other days) housed in a former sardine canning factory. Browse the riverside market stalls. Walk across the bridge for views of the Arade River.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for dinner in Portimão before catching the train back. The riverside area near the old fish market is famous for cheap, delicious grilled sardines.

meals.breakfast: Quick coffee and pastel de nata at Lagos train station café ~€2
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Praia da Rocha — grilled fish sandwich and local beer ~€7
meals.dinner: Portimão riverside — grilled sardines with bread and salad at a local tasca, one of the best budget meals in Portugal ~€8-10

day_by_day.notes: The Lagos-Portimão train runs frequently. Praia da Rocha gets busy on weekends but is quieter on Mondays. The sardine grills along Portimão riverside are legendary — don't miss them!

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle from a Lagos bike rental shop (~€10-12/day) and cycle along the Ecovia do Litoral coastal cycling path. Head east toward Luz and Burgau — charming whitewashed fishing villages with small beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Praia da Luz for a swim — a lovely sheltered bay with a relaxed village atmosphere. Explore Burgau village, one of the most authentic fishing villages in the western Algarve. Have a coffee at a local café.
day_by_day.evening: Cycle back to Lagos (or take a bus if tired — bikes can sometimes be loaded). Return the bike. Enjoy a relaxed evening in the hostel or a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or local café — yogurt, fruit, coffee ~€3
meals.lunch: Praia da Luz beach bar — fresh fish of the day with salad ~€9-11
meals.dinner: Burgau village restaurant or back in Lagos — Restaurante O Galeão for traditional cataplana ~€11-13

day_by_day.notes: The cycling route is mostly flat with some gentle hills. September is ideal for cycling — not too hot. Bring water, sunscreen, and a small backpack. Check bike rental shops near the marina.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting experience — visit Herdade dos Pimenteiros or arrange a visit to a local wine cooperative. Alternatively, join a budget wine tour departing from Lagos (~€25-35 including transport and tastings at 2-3 wineries). Book through the hostel or local tour operators.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the wine tour, visit the Mercado Municipal de Lagos for fresh local produce. Pick up local honey, almonds, figs, and carob — Algarve specialties. These make great budget snacks and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking night — use the hostel kitchen to prepare a simple Portuguese-inspired meal with market ingredients. Share with fellow hostel guests for a social evening.

meals.breakfast: Local padaria — fresh bread rolls with butter and coffee ~€2.50
meals.lunch: Included in wine tour, or light snacks at the winery
meals.dinner: Self-cooked hostel meal — grilled chicken, roasted vegetables, local wine ~€5-6 per person

day_by_day.notes: Ask the hostel reception about the best local wine tour operators — they often have discount deals. Algarve wines are underrated and very affordable compared to Douro or Alentejo wines.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — take the train from Lagos to Silves (~€3, 40 min). Visit the magnificent Castelo de Silves, a Moorish castle in excellent condition (€2.80 entry). Explore the medieval town and the Gothic cathedral (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Arade River in Silves. Visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia (~€2). Browse the local shops for handmade ceramics and cork products — great budget souvenirs. Silves is the historic capital of the Algarve and far less touristy than the coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by train. Evening walk along the Lagos waterfront. Enjoy a sundowner at a marina bar — many offer happy hour deals.

meals.breakfast: Café in Silves town center after arrival — coffee and local pastry ~€2.50
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — famous for seafood, try the cataplana for ~€12-14 (splurge-worthy)
meals.dinner: Back in Lagos — Tasca do Zé or similar local tasca — soup, bread, main course, wine for ~€9

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a hidden gem that most beach tourists skip. The castle views over the orange groves and river are spectacular. September is orange harvest season in the region.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Praia de Dona Ana — one of the most beautiful and photogenic beaches near Lagos, a 20-min walk from the hostel. Arrive early to get a good spot. Swim, snorkel, and explore the small sea caves accessible at low tide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the coastal path from Dona Ana to Praia do Camilo and back — stunning cliff scenery. Spend the afternoon relaxing on the beach. Rent a paddleboard (~€10/hr) for some fun on the water.
day_by_day.evening: Friday night out in Lagos! The town has a great nightlife scene. Start with dinner, then join the hostel pub crawl if available, or explore independently. Rua 25 de Abril and the marina area are the hubs.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local café — full breakfast ~€4-5
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Dona Ana — grilled chicken piri-piri and chips ~€8
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Vivant or similar — pizza or pasta for a change of pace ~€9-11

day_by_day.notes: Check tide times for Praia do Camilo — low tide reveals the best rock pools and cave access. The hostel may organize Friday night social events — great for meeting other travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — head to Meia Praia for a long, relaxed morning. This is the longest beach near Lagos (4km) and perfect for a final swim. Reflect on the trip and soak up the last of the Algarve sun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for some last-minute souvenir shopping. Visit the local market and shops for: local wine bottles (~€6-8), Algarve honey (~€4), handmade ceramics (~€5-10), cork products (~€3-8), and local almond sweets (Dom Rodrigo) (~€3). Pack your bags and organize for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Lagos — treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal to celebrate the trip. Visit Restaurante Adega da Marina or O Camilo for a proper sit-down seafood dinner. Share a bottle of local Algarve wine.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or local pastelaria — full Portuguese breakfast ~€4
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach snack bar — sandwich and fresh juice ~€6
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — grilled sea bass or lobster cataplana at a marina restaurant ~€15-18 (budget splurge for the last night)

day_by_day.notes: Pack souvenirs carefully — wine bottles need bubble wrap or wine bags (available at the airport). Check the hostel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for the last day.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Boutique Taghostel (store luggage if needed). Final morning walk through Lagos Old Town — visit any spots you missed. Grab a last pastel de nata and coffee at your favorite local café. Take photos of the city walls and harbor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time: take the Eva Bus or Rede Expressos from Lagos bus station to Faro Airport (~€5-7, ~1.5 hrs). Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight. Arrive at Faro Airport, check in, and browse the duty-free for last-minute Portuguese wine or port.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days in the Algarve — beaches, wine, history, and culture on a budget!

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and coffee in Lagos — a perfect farewell ~€2.50
meals.lunch: Light snack at Lagos bus station or Faro Airport café ~€5-7
meals.dinner: Airport or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding flights): Accommodation at Taghostel hostel dorm ~€15-25/night = ~€195-325. Food ~€20-25/day = ~€260-325. Transport ~€5-10/day = ~€65-130. Activities ~€5-10/day = ~€65-130. TOTAL ESTIMATE: ~€585-910 for 13 days. Very achievable on a budget!

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30. Travel from Faro Airport to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (~1 hour by taxi or pre-booked transfer). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival: Grab a light bite near the hostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva. A nearby tasca or late-night snack bar in Lagos old town is ideal. Unwind with a glass of local Algarve wine before bed.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In transit
meals.lunch: N/A – In transit or airport meal
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at a nearby tasca or café in Lagos old town – try a bifana (pork sandwich) or a simple prego roll with a local beer or wine (€8–12)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid waiting at night. Faro to Lagos by taxi costs approximately €60–80. Alternatively, a pre-arranged shuttle service (~€20–25 per person) is more budget-friendly. Keep Day 1 light – rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely breakfast at the hostel or a nearby café, take a gentle orientation walk through Lagos old town. Explore the historic city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone streets. Visit the Igreja de Santo António (Church of St. Anthony) with its stunning gilded baroque interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, Lagos's longest and most accessible beach (10-minute taxi or bus ride). Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and relaxing on the golden sands. The calm waters make it perfect for a first beach day. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella (~€10–15).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos town center. Stroll along the marina and watch the sunset over the Ponta da Bandeira Fort. Enjoy dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or a local pastelaria near the hostel – coffee, fresh pastéis de nata, and toast (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Meia Praia – grilled sardines, salad, and a cold Sagres beer (€12–16)
meals.dinner: O Camilo or a similar mid-range seafood restaurant in Lagos – try the grilled sea bass (robalo) or cataplana for two (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lagos old town is very walkable. The local bus (Eva Transportes) connects the town center to Meia Praia beach for under €2. September weather in the Algarve is typically warm (24–28°C) with minimal rain – ideal beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Take the **Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim** experience. Depart from Lagos by car or organized tour (~45 minutes east). This iconic hike along the Algarve's Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos) offers breathtaking views of dramatic limestone cliffs, hidden grottos, and turquoise coves. The trail from Praia da Marinha to Benagil is approximately 5.5 km one way.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, descend to Praia da Marinha itself – consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Swim in the crystal-clear waters surrounded by golden limestone arches and sea stacks. Explore the small sea caves accessible from the beach at low tide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed evening in the Rua 25 de Abril bar street area. Try a ginjinha (cherry liqueur) at a local bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hostel or a nearby café before departure – eggs, toast, fruit, and coffee (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks from a local supermarket (Pingo Doce) before the hike – sandwiches, fruit, water (€5–8). There are limited food options along the trail.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega Marina or similar in Lagos – try the açorda de marisco (seafood bread stew) or grilled octopus (€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy walking shoes and bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water for the coastal hike. The trail can be uneven and exposed. Start early (9:00–9:30 AM) to avoid midday heat and crowds. Check tide times before exploring sea caves. Distance from Lagos to Praia da Marinha: ~45 km – consider renting a car for the day (~€35–45) or joining an organized tour.

day_by_day.morning: Take the **Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour** – one of the Algarve's most iconic experiences. Depart from Benagil beach (accessible from Lagos by car, ~45 min). Paddle through the legendary Benagil Cave (Algar de Benagil), a cathedral-like sea cave with a natural skylight, accessible only by water. Tours typically last 2–3 hours and include stops at multiple sea caves and hidden beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on Praia de Benagil or nearby Praia do Carvalho. Enjoy a leisurely lunch at a local restaurant in Carvoeiro village (10-minute drive). Explore Carvoeiro's charming whitewashed village center and clifftop boardwalk (Passadiço do Caramujeira).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Visit the Mercado de Lagos (if open late) or browse local shops for souvenirs. Enjoy a sunset drink at a rooftop bar or terrace overlooking the town.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria near the hostel – coffee and croissant or tosta mista (€4–6)
meals.lunch: O Castelo restaurant in Carvoeiro or a similar terrace café – fresh fish of the day, salad, and local wine (€14–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco or similar tapas-style restaurant in Lagos – share several petiscos (Portuguese tapas) including chouriço, cheese, and seafood (€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil Kayak Tour in advance, especially in September when it remains popular. Tours typically cost €35–50 per person. Bring a waterproof bag for your phone and valuables. The cave is best visited in the morning when light streams through the natural skylight. If kayaking isn't preferred, stand-up paddleboard (SUP) tours are also available.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to **Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente** – the southwestern tip of Europe. Drive or take a bus from Lagos (~30 minutes). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres, a 15th-century fortress perched on a windswept promontory. Explore the historic wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos) and learn about Portugal's Age of Discovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Cabo de São Vicente (5 minutes from Sagres) – Europe's most southwesterly point. Stand at the edge of the continent with stunning Atlantic Ocean views. Explore the lighthouse and browse the small market stalls selling local crafts. Return to Sagres for a late lunch at a local restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Saturday evening is lively in the old town – enjoy the atmosphere of the Rua 25 de Abril area. Try a traditional Portuguese dinner followed by a nightcap at one of Lagos's popular bars.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hostel or a café in Lagos before departure (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Nortada in Sagres or a similar spot – fresh Atlantic fish, grilled to perfection, with local potatoes and salad (€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião in Lagos – a well-regarded mid-range restaurant known for traditional Algarvian cuisine; try the cataplana de peixe (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente can be windy even in September – bring a light jacket. The bus from Lagos to Sagres (Eva Transportes) runs several times daily and costs ~€4 each way. A rental car gives more flexibility to explore both sites. The lighthouse at Cabo de São Vicente is one of the most powerful in Europe.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning in Lagos. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and explore the Mercado Municipal de Lagos (Lagos Market) – a great Sunday morning activity to browse fresh local produce, cheeses, smoked meats, and regional specialties. Pick up some local snacks and wine for later.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia Dona Ana – one of Lagos's most picturesque beaches, just a 20-minute walk from the hostel. Surrounded by dramatic ochre cliffs and rock formations, it's ideal for swimming and snorkeling. Alternatively, rent a kayak or paddleboard directly from the beach (~€15/hour) to explore the nearby sea caves independently.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Ponta da Piedade cliffs (20-minute walk from Dona Ana beach) – arguably the most spectacular coastal scenery in the Algarve. Watch the golden hour light illuminate the limestone formations. Return to town for a relaxed Sunday dinner.

meals.breakfast: Slow breakfast at a café near the market – fresh bread, local cheese, presunto (cured ham), and coffee (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach with market purchases – local cheese, bread, fruit, and a bottle of Algarve white wine (€10–15 total)
meals.dinner: A Forja restaurant in Lagos or similar – traditional Sunday roast-style Portuguese meal; try the arroz de pato (duck rice) or leitão (suckling pig) if available (€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the late afternoon for golden hour photography. The cliffs are unfenced in places – exercise caution. Boat tours from Lagos marina to Ponta da Piedade grottos are also available (~€15–20 per person, 45 minutes) if you prefer to see the formations from the water.

day_by_day.morning: Take the **Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience** in the Lagoa wine region (~40 km east of Lagos). Visit a local winery for a guided tour of the vineyards and wine cellar. Learn about the unique Algarve wine-making tradition, including the indigenous Negra Mole and Crato Branco grape varieties. Enjoy a structured tasting of 4–6 wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: The experience continues with a traditional cataplana cooking demonstration and tasting lunch. The cataplana (a copper clam-shaped cooking vessel) is the signature dish of the Algarve – typically filled with seafood, pork, or vegetables slow-cooked with local spices. Pair with the wines tasted earlier.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos in the late afternoon. Enjoy a light evening given the indulgent lunch. Take a leisurely walk through the old town, visit the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos) if not yet visited, and enjoy a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near the hostel before departure – coffee, pastéis de nata, and fresh orange juice (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Included in the Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience – a full traditional cataplana meal paired with local wines
meals.dinner: Light dinner at a tasca in Lagos – soup (caldo verde), bread, and a simple grilled fish or cheese board (€10–14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience typically costs €55–75 per person and includes transportation from Lagos in some packages. Book in advance. The Lagoa wine region (DOC Lagoa) produces some of Portugal's most underrated wines. September is harvest season – you may get to see grape picking in action.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to **Silves** – the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve (~35 km northeast of Lagos). Begin the **Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk** experience. Explore the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves, one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal. Enjoy panoramic views over the orange groves and Arade River valley from the battlements.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the guided food walk through Silves old town. Sample local specialties including medronho (arbutus berry brandy), local cheeses, smoked sausages, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos), and fig-based confections. Visit the Gothic Silves Cathedral (Sé de Silves) and the Archaeological Museum. Browse the local market if it's running.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed evening – perhaps a wine bar visit to try more Algarve wines discovered during the tasting experience. Share a bottle with fellow travelers at the hostel's common area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hostel or a café in Lagos before departure (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Included in the Silves Food Walk – multiple tastings throughout the old town covering a full range of local flavors
meals.dinner: Restaurante Rui in Silves (if returning late) or back in Lagos – try the regional specialty of grilled chicken piri-piri or amêijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams in garlic and white wine) (€14–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is easily reached by train from Lagos (change at Tunes, ~1 hour, €5–7) or by car (~35 minutes). The Silves Medieval Fair (usually in August) may have just ended, but the town retains its historic charm year-round. The castle entrance fee is approximately €3. September is also the time of the Silves Beer Festival – check local listings.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at **Praia de Odeceixe** – a stunning and less-crowded beach where a river meets the Atlantic (~50 km north of Lagos, near the Alentejo border). The unique geography creates a natural lagoon on one side and ocean waves on the other, making it perfect for all swimming abilities. The drive through the Vicentine Coast Natural Park is scenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Odeceixe perched on the hillside above the beach. Browse the small artisan shops and enjoy the authentic, non-touristy atmosphere. Walk the short trail from the village down to the beach through eucalyptus and pine trees.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a well-deserved rest and a relaxed dinner in the old town. Try a different neighborhood restaurant you haven't visited yet.

meals.breakfast: Grab pastries and coffee to go from a local padaria (bakery) before the drive (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Odeceixe or a beach snack bar – fresh grilled fish, salad, and local wine with a view of the river and sea (€13–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Taberna de Lagos or a similar mid-range restaurant – try the bacalhau à brás (shredded salt cod with eggs and potatoes) or a hearty carne de porco à alentejana (pork with clams) (€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Odeceixe is best reached by car (~50 minutes from Lagos). The beach can get busy on weekends but is quieter on weekdays. The river lagoon side is calmer and ideal for families or those who prefer gentler swimming. Bring a picnic option as food choices near the beach are limited. Fill up the tank before heading north as petrol stations are sparse.

day_by_day.morning: Explore **Portimão and Praia da Rocha** (~20 km east of Lagos, easily reached by bus or train). Start with a visit to the Museu de Portimão – an excellent free museum housed in a former sardine canning factory, offering fascinating insight into the region's fishing and industrial heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Rocha – one of the Algarve's most famous beaches, with a wide golden sand bay backed by dramatic red cliffs. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing. Walk the clifftop promenade for panoramic views. Visit the small Fortaleza de Santa Catarina at the eastern end of the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Portimão's riverside dining scene along the Arade River. The area near the old fish market is known for excellent grilled sardines – a quintessential Algarve experience. Return to Lagos by bus or train in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hostel or a café in Lagos before departure (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Rocha – grilled sardines, salad, and a cold beer (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant in Portimão near the Largo 1° de Dezembro – try the famous Portimão sardines grilled over charcoal, served with boiled potatoes and peppers (€12–16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The train from Lagos to Portimão takes approximately 20 minutes and costs ~€2.50 each way – very convenient. Praia da Rocha is more developed and touristy than other beaches on this itinerary but worth visiting for its sheer scale and beauty. The Museu de Portimão is free on the first Sunday of each month.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or scooter in Lagos and explore the **Ria de Alvor** – a beautiful estuary and nature reserve just east of Lagos (~8 km). Cycle along the boardwalk trails through salt marshes and sand dunes, spotting flamingos, herons, and other migratory birds. September is excellent for birdwatching as migratory species pass through.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to **Praia de Alvor** – a wide, sheltered beach at the mouth of the estuary, popular with locals and ideal for a relaxed swim. The village of Alvor itself is charming, with a 16th-century Manueline church and a lively fish market. Browse the village and enjoy the authentic atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for your penultimate evening. Treat yourself to a slightly more special dinner to celebrate a wonderful trip. Visit a wine bar to try a final selection of Algarve and broader Portuguese wines.

meals.breakfast: Slow breakfast at a café in Lagos – full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, toast, cheese, ham, and coffee (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Tasca do Celso or a similar local restaurant in Alvor village – try the local specialty of percebes (barnacles) or lingueirão (razor clams) with local white wine (€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon (or similar upscale-casual option in Lagos) – a slightly splurge-worthy dinner with a tasting menu or à la carte selection of the best Algarvian cuisine; pair with a bottle of Algarve DOC wine (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bicycle rental in Lagos costs approximately €10–15/day. Scooter rental is ~€25–35/day and requires a valid driving license. The Ria de Alvor boardwalk is flat and easy to cycle. Alvor village is very photogenic – bring your camera. The estuary is a protected Natura 2000 site.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day – return to your favorite beach from the trip or try **Praia do Camilo**, a small and intimate beach just south of Lagos town (20-minute walk from the hostel). Accessed via a wooden staircase down the cliffs, it's one of the most beautiful small beaches in the area. Swim, snorkel, and soak up the last of the Algarve sun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for a final afternoon of souvenir shopping and exploration. Visit the local shops along Rua 25 de Abril and Rua Cândido dos Reis for ceramics, azulejo tiles, local wines, medronho, almond sweets, and other regional products. Pack your purchases carefully for the journey home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Lagos – choose your favorite restaurant from the trip or try somewhere new. Reflect on the highlights of 13 days in the Algarve over a final bottle of local wine. End the evening with a walk along the marina and a last look at the illuminated Ponta da Bandeira Fort.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near the hostel – coffee, fresh pastéis de nata, and juice (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach snack bar at Praia do Camilo or a café back in town (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Return to your favorite restaurant from the trip or try Restaurante Atlântico in Lagos – a final celebratory meal with the best of Algarvian seafood and wine (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Camilo is a short walk from the hostel – one of the most convenient and beautiful beaches in Lagos. September weekends can still be busy, so arrive early to secure a good spot. For souvenirs, local wine (Adega do Cantor, Quinta dos Vales) and almond-based sweets (Dom Rodrigos, morgados) make excellent gifts. Check baggage allowances before buying wine bottles.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at a favorite café. Take a final stroll through the old town, revisit any spots you loved, and say goodbye to the city. Check out of Boutique Taghostel (standard checkout is typically 11:00 AM – confirm with the hostel).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, transfer to Faro Airport (~1 hour from Lagos). Allow at least 2–2.5 hours before your flight for check-in and security. If time permits, stop in Faro old town (Cidade Velha) for a final coffee and a walk through the historic walled city near the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Carry the memories of 13 incredible days in the Algarve – dramatic cliffs, turquoise waters, sea caves, Moorish castles, and exceptional wine and food.

meals.breakfast: Final Portuguese breakfast at a café in Lagos – make it count with a full spread of coffee, pastéis de nata, fresh bread, cheese, and ham (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport or a café in Faro old town if time allows (€10–15)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Arrange your return transfer from Lagos to Faro Airport in advance. A taxi costs approximately €60–80; a shared shuttle is ~€20–25 per person. If your flight is in the evening, you can store luggage at the hostel and enjoy a final half-day in Lagos. Faro Airport (FAO) is small but efficient – allow adequate time for security. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and arches along the golden coastline, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's dramatic geology.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Visit a local winery in the Lagoa wine region, the heart of Algarve viticulture, for a guided tasting of regional wines including Arinto and Negra Mole varieties. Pair your wines with a traditional Cataplana seafood stew prepared by a local chef.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park spanning 60km of coastline. Discover barrier islands, flamingo colonies, and secluded barrier beaches only accessible by boat, with stops for swimming and snorkeling in calm lagoon waters.

experiences.name: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the Moorish red sandstone castle of Silves, the ancient Algarve capital, followed by a guided food walk through the historic old town. Sample local specialties including carob products, medronho brandy, almond sweets, and fresh orange juice at traditional market stalls.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer pre-arranged to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (approx. 1 hour drive). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome glass of local Algarve wine prepared by the hotel. Light room service or a curated welcome amenity basket awaits.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — arrival day
meals.lunch: Not applicable — arrival day
meals.dinner: Light in-room welcome amenity: local charcuterie, artisan cheeses, olives, and a bottle of chilled Algarve white wine arranged by the hotel

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer before departure. Confirm late check-in with Boutique Taghostel. Keep Day 1 completely relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel, then take a short stroll to explore Lagos Old Town — wander the historic city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone streets. Visit the Igreja de Santo António, a stunning baroque church, and the adjacent Municipal Museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, Lagos's longest and most elegant beach (10-minute taxi). Settle into a premium sun lounger with umbrella service. Swim in the calm Atlantic waters and enjoy the golden September sunshine. Optionally rent a paddleboard or kayak from the beach concession.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a sunset aperitivo at a rooftop bar overlooking the marina. Dinner at a top Lagos restaurant celebrating fresh Algarve seafood.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — fresh pastries, local honey, fruit, eggs, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch at Meia Praia Beach Club — grilled fish, fresh salads, and chilled local rosé
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina, Lagos — renowned for premium grilled fish, cataplana dishes, and an excellent Portuguese wine list

day_by_day.notes: September weather in the Algarve is typically warm (24–28°C) with minimal crowds compared to peak summer. Perfect beach conditions expected.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim experience. Depart from Lagos by private transfer (approx. 40 minutes east). Explore the dramatic limestone cliffs, hidden grottos, and sea caves of one of Europe's most photographed coastlines. Guided hike along the clifftop trail with expert commentary on geology and local flora.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Praia da Marinha beach for a private swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters. Explore the natural rock arches and sea caves accessible from the beach. Enjoy a packed premium picnic lunch prepared by the hotel or a nearby beach café.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Relax at the hotel with a spa treatment or in-room massage (pre-book with hotel). Dinner at a fine dining restaurant in Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Premium picnic basket prepared by the hotel or lunch at Restaurante Pescador near Carvoeiro — fresh catch of the day with local wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at No Pátio, Lagos — intimate fine dining with creative Portuguese cuisine and exceptional wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring sunscreen, a hat, and swimwear. The coastal hike is moderately easy but involves some uneven terrain. Private transfer recommended for comfort.

day_by_day.morning: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour. Private transfer to Benagil Beach (approx. 50 minutes from Lagos). Embark on a premium guided kayak tour through the world-famous Benagil Cave — a cathedral-like sea cave with a natural skylight. Paddle through sea arches and hidden grottoes along the Algarve's most spectacular coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on Praia de Benagil or nearby Praia do Carvalho. Enjoy the dramatic cliff scenery and calm September waters. Optional boat tour upgrade to explore additional caves along the coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Sunset drinks at the hotel terrace. Dinner at a premium restaurant in Carvoeiro or Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante O Castelo, Carvoeiro — elevated seafood with panoramic ocean views and local Lagoa wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at Casinha do Petisco, Lagos — beloved local gem with outstanding cataplana and grilled seafood, excellent wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil Kayak Tour in advance as it is extremely popular. Bring waterproof bags for cameras and valuables. The tour is suitable for all fitness levels with basic paddling instruction provided.

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience. Private transfer to the Lagoa wine region (approx. 45 minutes from Lagos). Visit a prestigious local winery for a guided tour of the vineyards and cellar. Learn about the unique Algarve terroir, indigenous grape varieties (Negra Mole, Crato Branco), and winemaking traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine experience with a structured tasting of premium Algarve wines — whites, rosés, reds, and a late-harvest dessert wine. Paired with a traditional Cataplana cooking demonstration and tasting lunch featuring the iconic copper pot dish filled with clams, prawns, and chorizo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos in the late afternoon. Stroll along the marina at golden hour. Light evening with cocktails at a stylish bar.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Included in the Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience — full Cataplana feast with wine pairings at the winery
meals.dinner: Light dinner at Taberna de Lagos — tapas-style Portuguese petiscos, local cheeses, cured meats, and a bottle of Alentejo red

day_by_day.notes: Confirm dietary requirements with the winery in advance. Private transfer is essential as wine tasting is involved. This is a full-day immersive experience — one of the trip highlights.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern tip of continental Europe. Private transfer (approx. 35 minutes from Lagos). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres, a 15th-century fortress perched on clifftops where Henry the Navigator planned Portugal's Age of Discovery. Walk to Cabo de São Vicente lighthouse for breathtaking Atlantic panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres village and its pristine beaches — Praia do Martinhal or Praia da Mareta. Enjoy a leisurely lunch at a premium seafood restaurant. Optional surfing lesson or stand-up paddleboarding at Sagres's world-class surf beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for sunset. Dinner at a top restaurant with a focus on fresh Atlantic fish.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Lunch at A Sagres Restaurant — exceptional fresh tuna, grilled sea bass, and local wines with ocean views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Bon Bon (Carvoeiro, Michelin-starred) — avant-garde Portuguese tasting menu with wine pairing (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: Cabo de São Vicente can be windy even in September — bring a light layer. Bon Bon is Michelin-starred and requires advance booking weeks ahead. This is the premium dining highlight of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk experience. Private transfer to Silves (approx. 30 minutes from Lagos). Explore the magnificent Moorish red sandstone castle — the finest in the Algarve — with a knowledgeable guide. Discover the history of Silves as the ancient Moorish capital of Al-Gharb, visit the Cathedral, and enjoy panoramic views over orange groves and vineyards.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided food walk through Silves Old Town — taste local specialties including medronho (arbutus berry spirit), almond sweets, smoked sausages, artisan cheeses, and traditional pastries at curated local producers and markets. Visit the Silves Municipal Market for a sensory immersion into Algarve food culture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Relaxed evening — spa, pool, or a sunset walk along Ponta da Piedade cliffs (10-minute taxi from hotel). Dinner in Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Tastings included in the Silves Food Walk — supplemented by a sit-down lunch at Restaurante Marisqueira Rui, Silves — legendary for grilled fish and shellfish
meals.dinner: Dinner at Vasco da Gama, Lagos — classic Portuguese fine dining, excellent bacalhau preparations and premium wine list

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a must-visit for history and culture lovers. The food walk is a wonderful complement to the wine tasting day earlier in the trip. Comfortable walking shoes recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour. Early private transfer to Faro (approx. 1 hour 15 minutes from Lagos). Board a premium private boat for a guided cruise through the Ria Formosa lagoon — a UNESCO-protected natural park spanning 60km of coastline. Spot flamingos, herons, and migratory birds in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: The boat tour continues to the barrier islands — disembark at Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) or Ilha de Tavira for a private beach experience on pristine, uncrowded Atlantic shores. Swim in the calm lagoon waters and enjoy a premium picnic lunch on the boat or beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Faro. Optional stroll through Faro's charming Old Town (Cidade Velha) and the bone chapel at Igreja do Carmo. Private transfer back to Lagos. Dinner in Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel (early, before departure)
meals.lunch: Premium picnic lunch served on the private boat — fresh seafood, local cheeses, fruit, and chilled Algarve white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Dois Irmãos, Faro (if staying later) or upon return to Lagos at Casinha do Petisco

day_by_day.notes: This is a full-day excursion requiring an early start. Private boat charter recommended for a luxury experience. Bring binoculars for birdwatching. September is excellent for migratory bird sightings.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning — sleep in and enjoy a late gourmet breakfast at the hotel. Spend the morning at Praia de Dona Ana, one of Lagos's most beautiful and iconic beaches (15-minute walk or short taxi from hotel). Dramatic golden cliffs, calm waters, and premium beach club facilities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private yacht charter from Lagos Marina for an afternoon sailing experience along the Ponta da Piedade coastline. Sail past the iconic golden rock formations, sea arches, and hidden grottos. Swim and snorkel in secluded coves accessible only by boat. Champagne and canapés served on board.
day_by_day.evening: Return to marina at sunset for golden hour photography of the cliffs. Dinner at a premium Lagos restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Extended late gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Champagne, canapés, and a light seafood spread served on the private yacht
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina, Lagos — premium grilled lobster, fresh fish, and an extensive Portuguese wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Private yacht charter should be booked in advance through the hotel concierge. Half-day afternoon charters are widely available from Lagos Marina. This is one of the most memorable experiences of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Tavira — the most elegant and romantic town in the Algarve. Private transfer (approx. 1 hour 45 minutes from Lagos). Explore the charming town with its Roman bridge, Moorish castle ruins, and 37 historic churches. Stroll along the Gilão River promenade and visit the covered market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry to Ilha de Tavira — a stunning barrier island with pristine beaches and calm lagoon waters. Enjoy the beach, swim, and relax in this tranquil setting far from the crowds. Explore the island's natural beauty before returning to Tavira by ferry.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Tavira before the private transfer back to Lagos, or return earlier for dinner in Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel (early departure)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Aquasul, Tavira — refined Portuguese cuisine with excellent fresh fish and local Algarve wines in an elegant setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Patio, Tavira — romantic courtyard setting, creative Portuguese menu, and superb wine list

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is often called the most beautiful town in the Algarve and is a wonderful contrast to the western Algarve's dramatic cliffs. The ferry to Ilha de Tavira runs frequently in September.

day_by_day.morning: Premium golf experience at one of the Algarve's world-class golf courses near Lagos — Palmares Golf (stunning ocean views, 27 holes) or Espiche Golf. Tee time arranged through hotel concierge. Enjoy a round on beautifully manicured fairways with Atlantic Ocean panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-golf lunch at the golf club restaurant. Return to Lagos for a relaxed afternoon — spa treatment at the hotel, shopping for premium Portuguese goods (cork products, azulejo tiles, local wines, artisan ceramics) in Lagos Old Town boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar. Special premium dinner to celebrate the penultimate full day of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Palmares Golf Club restaurant — light Mediterranean menu with panoramic ocean views
meals.dinner: Dinner at No Pátio, Lagos — tasting menu with premium wine pairing, celebrating the final days of the trip

day_by_day.notes: Golf tee times must be booked in advance, especially for Palmares which is one of the most sought-after courses in the Algarve. Non-golfers can enjoy a spa morning instead.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — return to a favorite beach from the trip (Praia de Dona Ana or Meia Praia recommended). Enjoy a leisurely swim, sunbathe, and soak in the last of the Algarve sunshine. Reflect on the journey over a fresh juice and pastry at a beachside café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for a final exploration of the city. Visit the Mercado Municipal de Lagos for last-minute gourmet souvenirs — local wines, medronho, almond products, and artisan goods. Enjoy a final afternoon coffee at a traditional pastelaria with a pastel de nata.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — the finest meal of the trip at a premium restaurant. Celebrate 13 days in the Algarve with a special tasting menu, exceptional Portuguese wines, and a memorable evening.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante O Camilo, Lagos — perched dramatically above the cliffs with stunning ocean views, exceptional fresh fish
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Restaurante Bon Bon, Carvoeiro (Michelin-starred) — full tasting menu with premium wine pairing (if not visited on Day 6) OR a private chef dinner arranged at the hotel

day_by_day.notes: Consider arranging a private chef dinner at the hotel for an intimate farewell experience. Purchase wine and local products at the market to bring home. Pack non-essential items tonight to ease tomorrow's departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning — enjoy a last gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel. Take a final walk through Lagos Old Town, say goodbye to the golden cliffs and Atlantic views. Check out of the hotel and arrange luggage storage if needed for a few final hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time — optional final coffee and pastry at a Lagos café, or a short visit to Ponta da Piedade viewpoint for one last look at the iconic Algarve cliffs. Private luxury transfer to Faro Airport arranged through the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. End of an exceptional 13-day premium Algarve experience.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — savor every bite
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Restaurante Nah Nah Bah, Lagos — relaxed gourmet burgers and local craft beer, or a final seafood lunch at a marina restaurant
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight — trip concludes

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before departure for the Faro Airport transfer plus check-in. Confirm private transfer booking the evening before. Keep one bottle of Algarve wine in checked luggage as a souvenir of the trip.

query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September from London
